newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes hold gains to end above $20/bbl.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes hold gains to end above $20/bbl.

text.p: Outright U.S. cash crude prices struck a bullish stance on Wednesday, driving above the $20.00 a barrel level for the duration of the session on the back of a surging gasoline market.
Benchmark September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing talked late at $20.25-35 a barrel, some 45 cents higher than the close on Tuesday.

Traders said crude's sharp rally was squarely the result of carryover support generated from the gasoline sector, where August NYMEX unleaded gasoline contracts advanced to a new contract high and closed just below 70.00 cents a gallon.
Statistics from both the industry American Petroleum Institute (API) and the U.S. government showed gasoline stocks declining last week, as well as a nearly 10 million barrel draw for crude stocks.
"Even if people don't believe the numbers, there is clearly a lot of bullishness for the August gasoline contract," said a trader.
Outright price rallying worked against a mostly steady Gulf grade market, where sweet and sour domestic parcels failed to adjust from Tuesday levels.
Midland/WTI sold 30 cents cheaper than September WTI in the morning, and later sold a penny stronger at 29 cents below benchmark.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James moved at premiums of 25 cents and 26 cents over September WTI. Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire traded hands at 20 cents under WTI, traders said.
On the sour side of deals, West Texas Sour/Midland barely attracted attention, selling at $1.35 under September WTI, according to refiners in the Gulf.

Eugene Island also sold on Wednesday, getting done at WTI -$1.30. WTI/Cushing Postings Plus gained the most ground, selling at $2.02 and $2.03, as a result of the evening out of the September/October spread, traders said.

Activity on the Iraqi front stood still for the crude markets, as the U.N. review of Baghdad's aid distribution plan proceeded without comment. U.N. officials continued to peg the date for the plan's approval at the end of the week.

Traders said indications point to Iraq swiftly submitting a new pricing formula for renewed oil sales once the plan is approved. Optimistic players believe Iraq could start lifting crude again in the first part of August, but others think late August is more likely.
